records.question: How much will my Apex plan pay per day towards the hospital room?
records.answer: Your Apex Health Shield (v2) plan will pay **Rs. 7,500 per day** toward the hospital room rent. This is the daily room‑rent sub‑limit specified in the policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: Is there a daily cap on intensive care charges in the Apex plan?
records.answer: No. In the Apex Health Shield Version 2 policy, ICU/ICCU charges are covered “up to Sum Insured” with no sub‑limit or daily cap. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: For how many days before admission does the Apex plan cover my medical expenses?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) covers pre‑hospitalisation expenses for **60 days prior to admission** (linked to the illness). [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: What is the most the Apex plan pays for an ambulance each time I am hospitalised?
records.answer: The Apex plan covers up to **Rs. 3,500** for road ambulance charges per hospitalisation. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How much does the Apex plan pay for Ayurveda and other AYUSH treatment?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) covers AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy) treatment up to **100 % of the sum insured** when the treatment is linked to an illness. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: Does the Apex plan put a limit on day care procedures?
records.answer: Yes.  The policy states that day‑care procedures are covered up to the sum insured, but only for an initial period of 30 days [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How long must I wait before the Apex plan pays for an illness that is not an accident?
records.answer: The Apex plan requires an initial waiting period of **30 days** before it will pay for any illness that is not an accidental bodily injury. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How many months do I have to wait for cataract surgery to be covered on the Apex plan?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) policy requires a **12‑month waiting period** before cataract surgery and treatment are covered. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: When can I claim for hernia or piles treatment on the Apex plan?
records.answer: Claims for hernia or piles treatment can be made only after the 24‑month waiting period has expired. The policy states that the waiting period for “Hernia, Hydrocele, Piles and Fistula” is 24 months, and no claim is admissible until that period ends. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: After how long does the Apex plan cover a joint replacement?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield plan requires a waiting period of **24 months** before it will cover a joint replacement surgery (unless the surgery is accidental). [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How long is the wait for conditions I already had when I bought the Apex plan?
records.answer: For conditions you already had at the time of purchasing the Apex Health Shield plan, the waiting period is **36 months** from the policy inception date. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: What is the most the Apex plan pays per eye for cataract surgery?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) covers cataract surgery up to **Rs. 60,000 per eye**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How often can I get a free annual health check-up on the Silver wellness plan?
records.answer: You can receive a free annual health check‑up once per year on the Harbor Wellness Silver plan. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1]

records.question: What is the biggest renewal discount I can earn through steps on the Gold wellness plan?
records.answer: The biggest renewal discount you can earn on the Harbor Wellness Gold plan through steps is **up to 20%** [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: How much worldwide emergency cover does the Gold wellness plan give?
records.answer: The Gold wellness plan includes worldwide emergency cover up to $50,000 [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.1].

records.question: What is the daily limit on ICU charges under the Harbor wellness plan?
records.answer: There is no daily limit on ICU charges under the Harbor Wellness plan. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: How much air ambulance cover does the Gold wellness plan include?
records.answer: The Gold wellness plan includes air ambulance coverage of up to Rs. 5 Lakhs per hospitalisation. [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.2]

records.question: How much does the critical illness rider pay out if I am diagnosed with cancer?
records.answer: The critical illness rider pays out **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** if you are diagnosed with cancer of specified severity. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: How many days must I survive after a heart attack to claim under the critical illness rider?
records.answer: You must survive **30 days** after a first heart attack (myocardial infarction) to be eligible to claim under the critical illness rider. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What does the critical illness rider pay for kidney failure needing dialysis?
records.answer: The critical illness rider pays **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for kidney failure requiring dialysis. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1]

records.question: What commission does an agent in the Silver tier earn?
records.answer: An agent in the Silver tier earns a 7% commission. [AGENT_GUIDE_FAKE p.1]

records.question: How far back does the Apex plan look when deciding if a condition was pre-existing?
records.answer: The Apex plan considers a condition pre‑existing if it was diagnosed, had signs or symptoms, or received medical advice or treatment within **36 months prior to policy inception** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].

records.question: How many days do I have to cancel the Apex plan and get my premium back after buying it?
records.answer: You have 15 days from the date you receive the policy schedule to cancel the Apex plan and receive a refund of your premium (subject to minimal administrative charges) [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5].

records.question: Will the Apex plan pay for cosmetic surgery?
records.answer: No. Cosmetic surgery is excluded from coverage unless it is reconstructive surgery following an accidental bodily injury. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Does the Apex plan pay if someone deliberately injures themselves?
records.answer: No. The policy excludes claims that arise from intentional self‑inflicted injury, suicide attempts, or hazardous adventure sports, and such claims are strictly non‑payable. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: How much does the Apex plan pay for maternity?
records.answer: The Apex Health Shield (v2) covers inpatient medical expenses for maternity (normal or cesarean delivery) up to **Rs. 50,000 per delivery** (maximum of 2 deliveries) after a waiting period of 24 months. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: Is surgery for weight loss covered by the Apex plan?
records.answer: No.  Surgery for weight loss (bariatric surgery) is excluded from coverage under the Apex Health Shield policy. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4]

records.question: How early must I tell the insurer before a planned hospital stay on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must notify the insurer at least **48 hours before** a planned admission at a network hospital. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: How soon must I report an emergency admission on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must provide notice of an emergency admission within 24 hours of the emergency hospitalisation or before discharge, whichever comes first. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: How long after I leave hospital do I have to send in my claim papers on the Apex plan?
records.answer: You must submit all required claim documents within **30 days of discharge** from the hospital. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.5]

records.question: Do older customers pay part of the bill themselves on the Apex plan?
records.answer: Yes. Under Version 2 of the Apex Health Shield, insured persons aged 65 years and above are required to pay a mandatory co‑payment of 10 % of each admissible claim. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: How much does my cover grow each year I make no claim on the Apex plan?
records.answer: Your cover increases by **20 % of the base Sum Insured for each claim‑free policy year** under Version 2, up to a maximum cumulative bonus of **100 % of the base Sum Insured**. This means that if you go a year without making a claim, your Sum Insured will be 1.20 × the previous year’s base amount, and this can continue until the total bonus reaches the full 100 % of the original base Sum Insured. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: What is the ceiling on the no-claim growth in cover on the Apex plan?
records.answer: The no‑claim growth in cover is capped at a maximum cumulative bonus of **100 % of the base Sum Insured**. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6]

records.question: Does the Harbor wellness plan make senior citizens pay a share of the bill?
records.answer: I do not have enough information in the provided policy documents to answer this question.

records.question: How do I cancel the Harbor wellness plan after buying it, within the free-look window?
records.answer:
To cancel your Harbor Wellness plan within the free‑look period, simply send a written notice of cancellation. The free‑look window is 15 days from the date the policy is delivered, so you must submit the written notice within that time frame.  

The policy states: “A period of 15 days from policy delivery is allowed as free‑look. The policyholder may cancel by sending written notice.” [HARBOR_WELLNESS_BROCHURE p.4]

records.question: How long is the initial waiting period on the critical illness rider?
records.answer: The initial waiting period on the Critical Illness Rider is 90 days from the policy’s inception. [SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.2]

records.question: On the Apex plan, how long must I stay in hospital for it to count as inpatient treatment, and what is the daily room limit?
records.answer:
The policy defines an **inpatient hospitalisation** as an admission that lasts for at least **24 consecutive hours** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
The daily allowance for room rent under Version 2 is **Rs. 7,500 per day** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2].

records.question: How does the Apex plan's definition of a pre-existing condition line up with the waiting period for such conditions?
records.answer:
The policy defines a pre‑existing disease (PED) as any condition, ailment or injury for which the insured had signs or symptoms, was diagnosed, or received medical advice or treatment within **36 months prior to policy inception**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.1].  
The waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception is also **36 months**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  

Thus, the definition of a pre‑existing condition directly matches the waiting period: both are based on a 36‑month look‑back period.

records.question: What waiting period and money limit does the Apex plan set for cataract surgery?
records.answer: The Apex plan specifies a 12‑month waiting period for cataract surgery and treatment, with a sub‑limit of Rs. 60,000 per eye. [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: How does the maternity waiting period on the Apex plan compare with its general initial waiting period?
records.answer:
The Apex Health Shield plan’s general initial waiting period for all illnesses (except accidental bodily injury) is **30 days** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3].  
In contrast, the maternity benefit has a waiting period of **24 months** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.4].  

Thus, the maternity waiting period is significantly longer—24 months versus 30 days.

records.question: What does the critical illness rider pay for a major organ transplant, and what extra donor cost does its endorsement add?
records.answer:
The critical illness rider pays **100 % of the Rider Sum Insured** for a major organ (or bone‑marrow) transplant[SPECIAL_RIDER_SCANNED p.1].  
Its endorsement adds coverage for **organ‑donor expenses up to Rs. 2,00,000**[APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].

records.question: Did the daily room rent limit on the Apex plan go up or down between the older and newer version?
records.answer: The daily room‑rent limit increased – it rose from Rs. 5,000 per day in the older version (v1) to Rs. 7,500 per day in the newer version (v2)[APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2][APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How did the number of days of pre-hospital cover change between the old and new Apex plan?
records.answer:
The pre‑hospitalisation cover was extended from **30 days prior to admission** in the old Apex Health Shield (v1) to **60 days prior to admission** in the new Apex Health Shield (v2) – effectively doubling the coverage period.  

- Old plan (v1): 30 days prior to admission [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.2]  
- New plan (v2): 60 days prior to admission [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.2]

records.question: How did the cataract waiting period change between the old and new Apex plan?
records.answer:
The cataract waiting period was shortened from **24 months in the old Apex Health Shield (v1)** to **12 months in the new Apex Health Shield (v2)**, effectively cutting the waiting period in half.  
[APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3]

records.question: Which version of the Apex plan has the shorter wait for conditions declared at purchase?
records.answer:
The Apex Health Shield Version 2 has the shorter waiting period for conditions declared at purchase.  
In Version 2 the waiting period for pre‑existing diseases declared at inception is 36 months, whereas in Version 1 it is 48 months [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.3] [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.3].

records.question: How did the co-payment for senior citizens change between the two Apex versions?
records.answer: The mandatory co‑payment for insured persons aged 65 years and older was **20 % of each admissible claim in Version 1** [APEX_HEALTH_V1 p.6]. In Version 2, this co‑payment was **reduced to 10 % of each admissible claim** [APEX_HEALTH_V2 p.6].
